identity: Excerpt from a psychological novel in high literary MSA - Abbas Mahmoud al-Aqqad, «سارة» (1938). Third-person analytic narration that anatomises the heroine سارة for the reader, alternating aphoristic essayistic assertions about her nature (وثنية في التدين، فراسة في أمر الجنسين، عبادتها لأوروبا) with short narrative episodes and dialogue turns with همام. Register: periodic, heavily و/ف-coordinated, fond of rhetorical anaphora (فإذا به... وإذا بها... وإذا هي...) and of long conditional periods. Punctuation stripped; the original line/paragraph breaks survive as <NL> and they are fine-grained here - single-word lines (ماذا / يجوز) and one-turn dialogue lines sit beside 79-token runs.
law: Mandatory and untouchable: the token before every <NL> and the final token close a sentence; an <NL> never carries one. Inside a run, a sentence ends where one independent predication closes and a NEW predication FRAME opens. BOUNDARY signals, strongest first: (1) asyndeton - two finite clauses with distinct subjects/frames and no و/ف/ثم/لكن linking them (هذا خطؤكم معشر الرجال | إن الفتيان...; ...المجامع العامة | لحق بها ليلة بدار الأوبرا); (2) أما...ف topic-shift, which always opens a sentence; (3) a completed statement followed by ف + a fresh conditional period (فإذا/فلو) or by و/ف + a new grammatical subject or new topic (والحق أن...أعجوبة | وكان همام يسمع...). NON-boundaries, however long the span: verbs coordinated under one subject; the entire apodosis chain of a single conditional (this author sustains 70-word periods without stopping); relative/صفة, حال, and لأن/حتى/كي/على شريطة أن subordination; appositives and resumptive topics (...وطور سيناء | هذه الوثنية في عالم الدين تراها...); asyndetic predicates chained to one overt subject (وهي وثنية... لا تؤمن... وشديدة الإيمان...); rhetorical anaphora inside one period (قريبة منه... قريبة منه...); and above all the speech-frame-to-quote junction, which is a colon and not a stop - قال لها همام وهي تحكي له حكايتها لقد حسب لك اعترافك is ONE sentence. Calibration this doc lands on: 84 sentences over 1574 words, mean about 18.7.
reasoning: (1) i=82: the priest-arc closes at فلم تجد غير هذه الخطيئة التي تجهلها; وقد نجت الخاطئة الصغيرة opens a new event with a new subject. Kept ثم ذهبت inside it - ثم chains the same subject. (2) P7 split at 150 (topic sentence, then explanatory فهي ليست كالمتدينة) and 177 (new simile frame ومثلها كمثل الطفل). REFUSED 187: وليس بالملوم two clauses later still refers to الطفل, so وآباؤه مع ذلك must sit inside the same running period. (3) P9: the لو-clause modifies فراسة and ولكنها تفطن answers not-by-instruction, so the contrast is tightly bound - 251 marked only lo; 266 gets med because وبعينها ذكاء shifts from perception verbs to a new nominal predication. (4) i=422 lo only: the aside about Menjou is general-present (كما هو بغيض) and فأراد returns to narrative past - a real register shift - but ف + a narrative consequence verb is normally comma-level in this author (cf. فقالت at 1612, فكادت at 1302, فخرجت at 1405, all left intact). (5) i=469 and i=488 are both asyndetic across a frame change - hi. (6) P18 triplet: broke 560 and 572 because each وإذا opens its own predication frame (he knows her / she feels / she is close). This is my least secure structural call; a comma-series for the crescendo is equally defensible, so both are med, not hi. (7) i=611: broke before فإذا أحست, then left the whole 69-word apodosis chain (خشيت...ولم تتهمه...بل اتهمت...ونشأت...واستسلمت) unsplit - it is one conditional. That run is my proof that this author sustains 70-word sentences, which is why I did NOT split the 79-word P46 tail (its dislocated topic وهذه التي تغفل is only resolved at تراها) nor the 50-word narrative chain in P48. (8) i=976: asyndeton across a person switch (you will weep / I do not ask) inside one quoted turn - Arabic rarely juxtaposes finite clauses without a connective inside a sentence. Same logic at 1374. (9) i=1057 lo only: two full conditional periods joined by ولكن. I judge sentence-initial ولكن likelier than not where both halves are heavy, but it is my single biggest open question; I marked every such instance lo (251, 1057) and declined the light ones (768, 923, 1421) so the grade can settle the rule. (10) i=1292 hi: asyndeton PLUS aspect shift, habitual يهزأ to specific past لحق بها ليلة, despite the shared subject. (11) i=1588 REFUSED: لا تؤمن is asyndetic but وشديدة الإيمان coordinates with it as a second predicate of وهي, so the asyndeton is predicate-chaining, not clause-juxtaposition. Same reason 1223 and 366 were refused: resumptive topic and apposition. (12) i=1138 REFUSED: وربما وقفت continues the same justification for the lighting-director joke; I broke only at 1158 before فإذا أحجم. i=1489 REFUSED for the reason 1195 was left whole - a 7-word premise plus ف-consequence is one breath. (13) Every dialogue frame junction (117, 430, 907, 955, 966, 1002, 1015, 1339, 1370, 1614, 1625) left unbroken on the colon rule. If the grade says otherwise, that single ruling flips about eleven sites at once, so it is the highest-value thing this batch can teach me.
